issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s suit to recover possession in a tenancy dispute governed by a law reserving that decision to a court cannot be referred to arbitration despite an arbitration agreement.
material_facts: The landlords sued to evict their tenants from a shop premises and sought other reliefs as well.
The tenancy agreement contained an arbitration clause covering disputes arising from the agreement.
The applicable tenancy law provided that, notwithstanding a contract, possession could be recovered only by an order or decree of the Civil Judge in a suit brought by the landlord.
issues.conclusion: The statutory restriction overrode the arbitration clause, so the possession-recovery suit could not be referred to arbitration under Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6 of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1997 overrides contrary contractual terms and reserves recovery of possession to the Civil Judge in a landlord’s suit. Section 2(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 preserves laws that make certain disputes non-arbitrable, and Section 8 does not require referral where such a statutory bar applies. Natraj Studios (P) Ltd. v. Navrang Studios supports the principle that statutory tenant protections and the exclusive jurisdiction conferred to enforce them prevail over an arbitration agreement. Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd. v. Pinkcity Midway Petroleums, Agri Gold Exims Ltd. v. Sri Lakshmi Knits & Wovens, and Branch Manager, Magma Leasing & Finance Ltd. v. Potluri Madhavilata were distinguished because they involved no comparable statutory bar to arbitration.

rule.if: landlord_tenant_dispute and possession_recovery_suit and statutory_protection_against_eviction and law_reserves_possession_decision_to_court and arbitration_clause_exists

predicates.landlord_tenant_dispute: A landlord and a tenant are involved in the dispute.
predicates.possession_recovery_suit: The landlord brought a suit seeking recovery of possession from the tenant.
predicates.statutory_protection_against_eviction: A law provides the tenant protection against eviction.
predicates.law_reserves_possession_decision_to_cour: The law reserves a decision granting recovery of possession to a court despite contrary contractual terms.
predicates.arbitration_clause_exists: The parties’ agreement contains a clause for arbitration of disputes.

issues.definition: When a landlord brings a possession-recovery suit against a tenant protected by law that reserves the possession decision to a court, the dispute is not referable to arbitration even if the parties have an arbitration clause.

issues.legal_issue: When a tenancy suit principally seeks eviction and also seeks related reliefs, the competent civil court may decide the other claims in that suit.
material_facts: The landlords’ suit principally sought eviction and also sought arrears of rent, municipal taxes, mesne profits, and a permanent injunction.
The court explained that the Civil Judge having jurisdiction meant the Civil Judge with jurisdiction to grant those additional reliefs.
issues.conclusion: The competent Civil Judge could hear and decide the suit, including the claims for arrears, mesne profits, and injunction, along with the eviction claim.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6 of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1997 assigns recovery of possession to the Civil Judge having jurisdiction in a landlord’s suit. The Court construed that expression to mean the Civil Judge with jurisdiction to grant the other reliefs claimed in the same suit.

predicates.tenancy_suit: A landlord brought a suit against a tenant concerning the tenancy.
predicates.eviction_is_primary_relief: The principal relief sought in the suit is eviction or recovery of possession.
predicates.related_claims_are_joined: The same suit also includes claims for related reliefs such as rent, taxes, mesne profits, or an injunction.

issues.definition: When a tenancy suit principally seeks eviction and joins related claims, the competent civil court may decide all those claims in the same suit.
